propositions: Point-in-time code-health metrics (coverage, complexity, clone count) have no durable trend series today and must be persisted as append-only NDJSON records for historical analysis.
Snapshot file must be stored under .rebar/ (a tracked directory) and negation-rule-added to .gitignore so it persists in git; storing under gitignored /reports/ would silently break the accumulation.
write_snapshot() appends timestamped metric records; read_snapshots(since, until) yields records within a date range and returns unavailable until a snapshot exists.
Malformed or truncated NDJSON lines are skipped without raising an exception, allowing partial corruption to not break the reader.
Round-trip unit tests verify write-then-read consistency, range filtering correctness, corruption resilience, and git-track-ability of the snapshot store path.
